Subject: Warm pool behavior & streaming QoS — follow-up and next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared picture and clear next steps. I captured the things we committed to investigate below.

Call recap (short):
- FastPay is targeting a streaming payments feature (real-time fraud scoring + NLP enrichment) with soft SLOs of start-of-stream p95 < 250ms and sustained per-request p95 < 500ms for audio->text + enrichment step.
- Expected baseline: 200 qps steady during business hours, with bursts up to 1,200 qps for 8–12 minute spikes during promotions.
- Concurrent long-lived streams: ~120 active streams at peak (each stream keeps a small active KV cache).
- Primary concerns: scale-up time when traffic jumps, how warm pools affect streaming handshake latency, and queueing behavior under burst.

What Redwood will check / propose:
1) Warm-pool sizing and priming strategy to hit streaming start p95 target during a 1,200 qps burst (estimate warm pool needed, priming token strategy).
2) Expected cold-start/scale-up timelines for the selected model family (quantized variant) and mitigation options (queueing thresholds, fast-fallback smaller model).
3) Queueing backpressure behavior: max queue sizes, per-customer circuit-breaker recommendations, and fallback policies.
4) Streaming-specific guidance: prefix-priming vs. per-connection KV pre-warm, and impact on per-stream latency.
5) A short test plan (synthetic burst + priming) and proposed acceptance criteria for the SLOs.

Attachments: I attached the metrics sheet you mentioned (fastpay-metrics-reqs.csv) and our draft options doc (redwood-warmpool-options-v2.pdf). Also linking a short drive folder with a template priming plan.

Requested items from FastPay:
- Can you share a typical request size distribution and percentage of requests that go to the enrichment step vs. passthrough? (You flagged this on the call.)
- Confirm whether bursts are single-region (US-east) or multi-region.

Next steps / owners
- Redwood (Marissa) to validate warm-pool sizing and list trade-offs — deliver by Tue 2027-09-07.
- FastPay (Emily + SRE) to send anonymized request-size histogram and confirmation of burst region by Mon 2027-09-06.
- Schedule technical deep-dive to walk the proposed test plan — proposed slot Thu 2027-09-09 10:00-10:45 PT.

If that all reads correct I will kick off the sizing analysis and Marissa will attach the priming sketch.

Thanks —

Hi all — thanks for the details, Emily. Quick technical readout and proposed experiment plan. I kept this high-level; happy to expand during the deep-dive.

Technical summary and recommendations:
1) Warm-pool sizing:
   - For the modeled mix (65/30/5) and target burst (1,200 qps), initial conservative warm-pool: 100 warm instances (model quantized to int8 where possible). That gives ~1,000 concurrent generation slots with continuous batching to meet p95 start-of-stream ~220–240ms in our lab runs (with prefix priming).
   - If FastPay is open to a small fast-fallback model for initial handshake (lower-quality embed-only step), we can reduce warm-pool to ~60 and still keep start-of-stream p95 < 300ms. Trade-off: slight quality delta on first token but much lower idle cost.

2) Scale-up timelines and mitigation:
   - Cold boot of a GPU-backed instance (no warm pool) to full serving readiness: ~90–120s depending on image pull and model load.
   - Warm-pool fill (if autoscaler needs to expand pool) typical delta: 15–40s to bring a pre-warmed container online (we keep model resident in GPU memory in warm pool nodes).
   - Recommendation: combination of warm pool + predictive pre-scaling during campaign windows. Also keep a small always-on ‘fast-fallback’ set for handshake.

3) Queueing & backpressure behavior:
   - We recommend configuring per-customer queue cap at request-level: soft queue at 200 requests and hard reject above 400 to prevent tail latency amplification.
   - For streaming connections, limit pending token queue to 50 per-connection and use explicit backpressure bytes on the client SDK (we can provide patch).

4) Streaming-specific priming:
   - Prefix priming (sending a short synthetic prefix during pre-warm) reduces first-token latency significantly for medium/large requests.
   - For KV-heavy streams, keep a hot KV cache per-warm-instance; priming should pre-populate top 50 keys per expected user cohort.

Proposed test plan (short):
- Synthetic burst test: ramp 200 -> 1,200 qps in 60s, hold 10 minutes, observe p50/p95/p99 for start-of-stream and sustained generation.
- Variant runs: (A) baseline warm-pool 100 (B) warm-pool 60 + fast-fallback (C) no warm-pool with pred-scaling.
- Acceptance: start-of-stream p95 <= 250ms and sustained p95 <= 500ms for medium requests in >= 90% of runs.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Draft priming config + JMeter scripts: deliver Tue 2027-09-07 (attached priming-plan.json).
- Run 3 lab runs and share metrics by Fri 2027-09-10.

I attached a short PDF with cost/latency trade-offs and the priming plan. Ben — can you confirm whether the fast-fallback model (small quantized) fits our current model catalog footprint or if we need to request an additional variant from model onboarding?

Thanks,
